items.title: 24.3.2 Distinction between Primary, Secondary and Tertiary Amines

source_refs.note: Topic 24.3.2 with Quick Check 24.3, answered (PDF 123-124). The book's secondary-amine equation is drawn with a garbled 'NH-HNO2'; it is written correctly here. Answers need review.

blocks.text: Primary, secondary and tertiary aliphatic amines are distinguished by their reactions with nitrous acid (nitric(III) acid), HNO2. Nitrous acid is unstable, so it is made in the mixture from sodium nitrite and hydrochloric acid: NaNO2 + HCl -> HNO2 + NaCl.

items: Primary amines form diazonium salts (diazotisation): CH3CH2NH2 + HNO2 + HCl -> CH3CH2N2+ Cl- + 2H2O. With nitrous acid, primary amines give off nitrogen gas, seen as bubbles.
Secondary amines form N-nitrosoamines, yellow oily liquids: CH3CH2NHCH3 + HNO2 -> CH3CH2N(CH3)-N=O + H2O (N-methyl-N-nitrosoethanamine).
Tertiary amines react to form a soluble nitrite salt, with no visible sign of reaction: CH3CH2N(CH3)2 + HNO2 -> [CH3CH2NH(CH3)2]+ NO2- (N,N-dimethylethanammonium nitrite).

blocks.alt: Top: NaNO2 + HCl -> HNO2 + NaCl, made cold. Then three panels: primary, CH3CH2NH2 + HNO2 + HCl gives CH3CH2N2+ Cl- + 2H2O, which breaks down at once giving N2 (bubbles); secondary, CH3CH2NHCH3 + HNO2 gives CH3CH2N(CH3)-N=O + H2O (yellow oily liquid); tertiary, CH3CH2N(CH3)2 + HNO2 gives [CH3CH2NH(CH3)2]+ NO2- (no visible change).
blocks.caption: Primary, secondary and tertiary amines with nitrous acid (original summary of the book's equations).
blocks.long_description: The three classes of amine give three different results with nitrous acid: bubbles of nitrogen for a primary aliphatic amine, a yellow oil for a secondary amine and no visible change for a tertiary amine, which simply forms a soluble salt.
